questions.text: What movie is the following quote from? 'The thing with ..... is, it's like the sun shines on you, and it's glorious. And then he forgets you, and it's very, very cold.'
questions.funfact: The Talented Mr. Ripley (1999) was directed by Anthony Minghella and based on Patricia Highsmith's 1955 novel. It stars Matt Damon, Jude Law, Gwyneth Paltrow and Cate Blanchett, and Jude Law earned an Oscar nomination for playing the charming Dickie Greenleaf.

questions.text: Which of these European countries currently has a volcano that is erupting?
questions.funfact: Italy's Mount Etna in Sicily is Europe's tallest active volcano at about 3,300 metres, and Stromboli, off the Italian coast, has been erupting almost constantly for centuries, earning it the nickname 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean'.

questions.text: The French term 'cul de sac' literally translates to the name of where Bilbo and Frodo live in the Shire in The Lord of the Rings. What is it?
questions.funfact: 'Cul de sac' is French for 'bottom of the bag', which is what 'Bag End' means in English. Tolkien took the name from Bag End, the Worcestershire farm that belonged to his aunt Jane Neave.

questions.text: Nike is the Greek goddess of what?
questions.funfact: Nike was the winged Greek goddess of victory, and the Romans called her Victoria. The sportswear brand took her name in 1971, and its Swoosh logo was designed by student Carolyn Davidson, who was paid just $35.

questions.text: In Blackjack, the dealer must keep taking cards until their hand reaches at least what number?
questions.funfact: Dealers must hit on 16 or lower and stand on 17 or higher, so they have no choice to make. Some casinos make the dealer hit on a 'soft 17', a hand that counts an ace as 11, which slightly improves the house's edge.

questions.text: What is the main ingredient used to make miso?
questions.funfact: Miso is a Japanese paste made by fermenting soybeans with salt and koji, a mould, and sometimes rice or barley too. It has been a staple of Japanese cooking for well over a thousand years.

questions.text: What do fans of Lady Gaga call themselves?
questions.funfact: Lady Gaga calls her fans her 'Little Monsters' and herself 'Mother Monster'. Beyoncé's fans are the Beyhive and Nicki Minaj's fans are the Barbz.

questions.text: What colour is the sunset on Mars?
questions.funfact: Mars's thin, dusty atmosphere scatters blue light towards you around the setting sun, so Martian sunsets glow blue, the opposite of Earth's red ones. NASA's Spirit rover photographed one in 2005.

questions.text: Haiti declared independence in 1804 from which country?
questions.funfact: Haiti's revolution, the first country founded by formerly enslaved people ended French rule, and independence was declared on 1 January 1804. The United States later occupied Haiti from 1915 to 1934.

questions.text: Guess the year: Hot Fuzz was released, J.K. Rowling released the final Harry Potter book, and the Soulja Boy song 'Crank That' was released.
questions.funfact: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows came out on 21 July 2007 and sold about 8.3 million copies in the US in its first 24 hours, a record at the time. 'Crank That (Soulja Boy)' reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 that year, after the 17-year-old shared it online himself.

questions.text: What does the T stand for in ATM?
questions.funfact: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. The first one was installed by Barclays in Enfield, north London, in June 1967 and was invented by John Shepherd-Barron. Its first customer was the actor Reg Varney.

questions.text: What two-word Gen Z term is used when someone shows off the outfit they're wearing so others can rate it?
questions.funfact: A 'fit check' is when someone shows off their outfit, often in a mirror video on TikTok or Instagram, for others to rate. 'Fit' is short for outfit, and 'drip' is Gen Z slang for stylish clothes.

questions.text: What do you call a tennis shot hit between your legs that starts with the letter T?
questions.funfact: A tweener is also known as a 'hot dog'. One of the most famous was Roger Federer's between-the-legs winner against Novak Djokovic in the 2009 US Open semi-final, which he went on to win.

questions.text: Which of these actresses has never won an Oscar for playing a real person?
questions.funfact: Olivia Colman won for playing Queen Anne in The Favourite, Meryl Streep for Margaret Thatcher in The Iron Lady, and Helen Mirren for Queen Elizabeth II in The Queen. Emma Stone's two Oscars, for La La Land and Poor Things, were both for fictional characters.

questions.text: Five countries in the world end with the letter L in English. Name all 5.
questions.funfact: Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that isn't a rectangle or square, and is made of two stacked triangular pennants. Brazil is the largest country in South America, and Portugal is one of the oldest nation states in Europe.

questions.text: Which artist had a breakout album with Stick Season and released The Great Divide in 2026?
questions.funfact: Noah Kahan is from Vermont, and 'stick season' is the bare stretch between the autumn leaves falling and the winter snow. The album came out in October 2022 and its title track became a hit in 2023, and The Great Divide followed in April 2026.

questions.text: Complete the next 4 words: '123 take my hand and come with me because you look so fine that I really... '
questions.funfact: The track voted number one in the 2003 Triple J Hottest 100

questions.text: Which sea mammal has the densest fur of any animal?
questions.funfact: A sea otter can have up to around a million hairs on a single square inch of skin. It has no blubber, so that thick fur traps a layer of air to keep it warm in cold water.

questions.text: Name a skincare brand or a bottled water brand whose names are anagrams of each other. (Only need to name one or the other)
questions.funfact: Nivea takes its name from the Latin 'niveus', meaning snow-white, and Evian water comes from Évian-les-Bains in France.

questions.text: Odd one out: for which of these nationalities has there never been an actor to play James Bond in the official films?
questions.funfact: Sean Connery was Scottish, George Lazenby is Australian, Pierce Brosnan is Irish, Timothy Dalton is Welsh, and Roger Moore and Daniel Craig are English. No Canadian has played Bond in the official films.

questions.text: 'Confabulate' has 3 main meanings. Which of these is NOT one of them?
options: To dress both fabulously and confusingly at the same time
questions.funfact: 'Confabulate' comes from the Latin 'confabulari', meaning to talk together. In psychology it means unknowingly filling memory gaps with made-up details, and AI researchers use it for chatbots that confidently produce false information.

questions.text: What word describes the noise made when a cork is drawn from a bottle?
questions.funfact: 'Cloop' is a real word for the pop of a cork leaving a bottle. The other two options were made up.

questions.text: Which Muppet was the first to have real human hands?
questions.funfact: The Swedish Chef has real human hands instead of felt puppet ones, which is why he can handle pots, pans and the odd chicken. His 'Swedish' is mostly gibberish, and he first appeared in 1975.

questions.text: Which country did the phrase 'daylight robbery' originally come from?
questions.funfact: The phrase comes from England's window tax of 1696, when people bricked up windows to avoid paying the tax. The phrase started out as a British expression and is now used to describe anything wildly overpriced.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Danielle for this question!

questions.text: If I have 200, add 10%, and then take away 10% of the new total, what am I left with? (Digits only)
questions.funfact: Adding 10% gives 220, and 10% of 220 is 22, which leaves 198. A rise and an equal fall in percentage always leaves you with 99% of where you started.

questions.text: What movie is the following quote from? 'I volunteer! I volunteer as tribute!'
options: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
questions.funfact: Katniss Everdeen, played by Jennifer Lawrence, says the line in The Hunger Games (2012) to take the place of her younger sister Prim after Prim's name is drawn at the reaping.

questions.text: Which actor has just been announced as the new James Bond?
questions.funfact: Robert Pattinson was unveiled on 16 November 2026 as the seventh actor to play 007, taking over from Daniel Craig. Denis Villeneuve is directing the film.

questions.text: What does 'El Camino' mean in Spanish?
questions.funfact: The Camino de Santiago, or Way of St James, is a network of pilgrimage routes that ends at the cathedral in Santiago de Compostela, Spain. Chevrolet's El Camino car-truck first appeared in 1959, and the 2019 Breaking Bad film is also called El Camino.

questions.text: Where on your body would you wear a fascinator?
questions.funfact: A fascinator is a decorative headpiece worn on a headband, clip or comb instead of covering the whole head like a hat. It is a race-day staple, with the Melbourne Cup and Royal Ascot among the best-known places to spot them.

questions.text: What colour was Andy's iconic 'lumpy' jumper in The Devil Wears Prada?
questions.funfact: In the 2006 film, Meryl Streep's Miranda Priestly explains that cerulean showed up in Oscar de la Renta gowns and Yves Saint Laurent jackets before trickling down to the clearance-bin sweater Andy was wearing.

questions.text: How many gherkin (pickle) slices are on a standard Big Mac?
questions.funfact: McDonald's UK says a Big Mac has two pickle slices, the same as a Quarter Pounder, while a Hamburger gets one.

questions.text: In which TV sitcom did all of these celebrities make a cameo: Michelle Obama, One Direction, Jack Black and Emma Stone?
questions.funfact: Michelle Obama played herself in 'iMeet the First Lady', One Direction appeared in 'iGo One Direction', and Jack Black played Spencer's online rival in 'iStart a Fan War'. Emma Stone also popped up in a small guest role.

questions.text: Which planet rotates on its side?
questions.funfact: Uranus is tilted by about 98 degrees, so it rolls around the Sun like a ball. Scientists think a giant collision early in the solar system's history knocked it over. Venus is the planet that spins backwards.

questions.text: Which country has the largest proportion of its population living in or around its capital city, excluding city-states?
questions.funfact: Qatar has upwards of 80% of its population that live in or around Doha.

questions.text: Guess the year: Kylian Mbappé was born, the Good Friday Agreement was signed in Northern Ireland, and Lauryn Hill released The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill.
questions.funfact: The Good Friday Agreement was signed on 10 April 1998 and largely ended the Troubles in Northern Ireland. Mbappé was born on 20 December 1998, and Lauryn Hill's debut solo album released in 1998 won five Grammys in 1999, including Album of the Year.

questions.text: What does the B stand for in FBI?
questions.funfact: FBI stands for Federal Bureau of Investigation. It began in 1908 as the Bureau of Investigation and took its current name in 1935.

questions.text: What do you call a word that blends the sounds and meanings of two words into one, like breakfast + lunch = brunch? (Hint: begins with P)
questions.funfact: Lewis Carroll popularised the term for words in Through the Looking-Glass (1871), where Humpty Dumpty compares a blended word to a suitcase with two meanings packed into it. A portmanteau is originally a type of travelling bag.

questions.text: What do you call three strikes in a row in bowling?
questions.funfact: A perfect game in ten-pin bowling is 12 strikes in a row, for a score of 300. Four strikes in a row is sometimes called a 'hambone'.

questions.text: Which of these famous figures does NOT appear in Homer's Odyssey?
questions.funfact: In the Odyssey, Odysseus blinds the Cyclops Polyphemus, resists the Sirens' song and spends a year with the enchantress Circe. Medusa belongs to the myth of Perseus instead.

questions.text: Name the top 5 best-selling car brands/ badges in the world for 2026. Hint: 3 of them are Asian.

acceptedAnswers.text: Is a piano considered part of a standard orchestra?
acceptedAnswers.funfact: A standard orchestra has strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion. The piano is not a permanent member and only joins when a piece calls for it, such as Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue, or as the solo instrument in a concerto.

acceptedAnswers.text: Complete the next 5 words: 'Don't stop, never give up/ Hold your head high and reach the top/ Let the world see what you have got/ Bring...'
acceptedAnswers.funfact: 'Bring It All Back' was S Club 7's debut single, released in 1999. The group also starred in TV series including Miami 7 and L.A. 7.

acceptedAnswers.text: Honey is made by bees from which substance that they collect from flowers?
acceptedAnswers.funfact: Worker bees swallow nectar, pass it between each other, then fan it with their wings until the water evaporates and it thickens into honey. A single worker bee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in their whole life.

acceptedAnswers.text: What does the 'i' in iPhone stand for?
acceptedAnswers.funfact: When Steve Jobs launched the iMac in 1998, he said the 'i' stood for 'internet', and also for individual, instruct, inform and inspire.

acceptedAnswers.text: Which of these is NOT a real animal from Australia?
acceptedAnswers.funfact: Pademelons are small wallabies, wallaroos sit between kangaroos and wallabies in size, and quokkas are famous for looking like they're smiling. Drop bears are a tall tale told to tourists, though the Australian Museum has happily played along.

acceptedAnswers.text: The narrow triangles on a backgammon board are called points. How many are there altogether on a backgammon board? (Digits only)
acceptedAnswers.funfact: A backgammon board has 24 points, split into four quadrants of six, and each player starts with 15 checkers. The dots on the dice, and the count of how far you still have to move, are what are called pips.

acceptedAnswers.text: What word can fill the blank to make three new words: eyes_____, _____spotter, over_____
acceptedAnswers.funfact: Eyestrain, trainspotter and overtrain all work. Trainspotting, the hobby of logging locomotive numbers, also gave its name to Irvine Welsh's 1993 novel.

acceptedAnswers.text: What colour are jeans before they have been treated?
acceptedAnswers.funfact: Raw cotton is a creamy off-white, so truly undyed denim looks cream or ecru. The classic blue comes from indigo dye, and 'raw' or 'dry' denim is dyed but simply never washed.

acceptedAnswers.text: What type of meat is used in a traditional cottage pie?
acceptedAnswers.funfact: Cottage pie is minced beef topped with mashed potato. The same dish made with lamb is a shepherd's pie.

acceptedAnswers.text: 0.6 (decimal) of an hour is how many minutes? (Digits only)

questions.text: Which TV series does the following quote come from? 'You come at the king, you best not miss.'
questions.funfact: The line is spoken by Omar Little, the shotgun-toting stick-up man played by Michael K. Williams in The Wire. Omar is one of television's best-loved characters and was famously a favourite of President Barack Obama.

questions.text: Jensen Huang has just been ousted as CEO of which major tech company?
questions.funfact: Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led it as CEO from the start. On 12 November 2026 Nvidia announced he was stepping down and leaving the board, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. Reports differ on whether he resigned or was pushed out.

questions.text: Namaste is a greeting in what language?
questions.funfact: Namaste comes from Sanskrit, where 'namas' means to bow and 'te' means 'to you', so it roughly means 'I bow to you'. It is used across India and Nepal, usually with the palms pressed together.

questions.text: What instrument is used to measure radiation?
questions.funfact: The Geiger counter grew out of work by Hans Geiger and Ernest Rutherford in 1908, and Walther Müller improved it into the Geiger-Müller tube in 1928. It clicks each time radiation ionises the gas inside the tube.

questions.text: Which of these is the first of the Ten Commandments in most Christian traditions?
options: You shall have no other gods before me
questions.funfact: Many Christian traditions count 'no other gods before me' as the first commandment. Jewish tradition counts 'I am the Lord your God' as the first, so the numbering varies between faiths.

questions.text: Which meat is traditionally used in a Reuben sandwich?
questions.funfact: A Reuben is corned beef with Swiss cheese, sauerkraut and Russian dressing, grilled on rye bread. Its origin is disputed between Omaha, Nebraska, and New York City, and a pastrami version is also popular.

questions.text: Which of these reality TV shows started first?
options: The Real Housewives of Orange County
questions.funfact: Big Brother began in the Netherlands in 1999, created by John de Mol. Love Island and Come Dine With Me both started in the UK in 2005, and The Real Housewives of Orange County followed in 2006.

questions.text: What is the scientific name for the knee cap?
questions.funfact: The patella is the largest sesamoid bone in the body, meaning it is embedded in a tendon. The word is Latin for 'small plate', and babies are born with a knee cap that is mostly cartilage, which turns to bone over the first few years of life.

questions.text: Which city was the first to host the modern Summer Olympics three times?
questions.funfact: London hosted in 1908, 1948 and 2012. Paris matched it in 2024 after hosting in 1900 and 1924, and Los Angeles will reach three in 2028 after 1932 and 1984.

questions.text: Guess the year: Gangnam Style went viral on YouTube, London hosted the Summer Olympics, and Felix Baumgartner jumped to Earth from the edge of space.
questions.funfact: Gangnam Style became the first YouTube video to pass one billion views in December 2012. On 14 October 2012, Felix Baumgartner's Red Bull Stratos jump from about 39 kilometres up made him the first person to break the sound barrier in freefall.

questions.text: What does the F stand for in SPF on sunscreen?
questions.funfact: SPF stands for Sun Protection Factor and measures protection against UVB rays, the ones that cause sunburn. SPF 30 blocks roughly 97% of UVB and SPF 50 about 98%. The scale was devised by Austrian chemist Franz Greiter in 1962.

questions.text: Finish the saying: 'The devil is in the ____'
questions.funfact: An older version of the saying is 'God is in the details', often linked to the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe. The devil version suggests that small details can cause big problems.

questions.text: Which UK TV show launched the careers of Nicholas Hoult, Dev Patel, Daniel Kaluuya and Jack O'Connell?
questions.funfact: Skins aired on E4 from 2007 to 2013 and became a launchpad for young actors. Dev Patel was cast in Slumdog Millionaire straight after, and Daniel Kaluuya later won an Oscar for Judas and the Black Messiah.

questions.text: Which book won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction?
options: Stag Dance: A Quartet by Torrey Peters
questions.funfact: Angel Down is by Daniel Kraus and published by Atria Books. Kraus also co-wrote the novel of The Shape of Water with Guillermo del Toro.

questions.text: Martin Scorsese and Leonardo DiCaprio have made 6 films together, starting with Gangs of New York in 2002. Name the next 5.
questions.funfact: Gangs of New York came out in December 2002. The Departed (2006) won Scorsese his first Best Director Oscar and also took Best Picture.

questions.text: Where is Rihanna from?
questions.funfact: Rihanna was born in Saint Michael, Barbados. In 2021, as Barbados became a republic, she was officially named a National Hero of the country.

questions.text: Which soul singer recorded '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' in 1967?
questions.funfact: Redding recorded the song just days before he died in a plane crash on 10 December 1967, aged 26. Released in 1968, it became the first posthumous number one on the US Billboard Hot 100.

questions.text: What is a male duck called, which is also the name of a popular Canadian music artist?
questions.funfact: A male duck is a drake, and a female is a duck or hen. A gander is a male goose, a cob is a male swan and a tom is a male turkey.

questions.text: What kind of car does Mr Bean drive?
questions.funfact: Mr Bean drives a lime-green British Leyland Mini 1000. His nemesis on the road is a blue Reliant Regal, the three-wheeler that keeps getting flipped over. Rowan Atkinson is a genuine car enthusiast and racer.

questions.text: 'She sells seashells by the seashore.' Which word best describes the repeated 's' sounds in this sentence?
questions.funfact: Sibilance is the repeated hissing of 's' and 'sh' sounds. The tongue twister is often linked to fossil hunter Mary Anning, though that connection is disputed, and it was popularised by a 1908 music-hall song.

questions.text: Which is the most southern national capital city in the world?
questions.funfact: Wellington sits at about 41 degrees south, making it the world's southernmost capital of a sovereign state. Canberra is further north at about 35 degrees south.

questions.text: What word can fit these three blanks to create three new words: Now___, ___by, ___tics
questions.funfact: Nowhere, hereby and heretics all work. 'Heretic' comes from a Greek word meaning 'able to choose'.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of different calendar days that can exist at the same time somewhere on Earth?
questions.funfact: Time zones run from UTC-12 to UTC+14, so for two hours each day, from 10:00 to 12:00 UTC, three different dates exist at once. Kiribati's Line Islands at UTC+14 are among the first places on Earth to see a new day.

questions.text: What is the name of Lin-Manuel Miranda's upcoming Broadway musical, set to open in New York in April 2027, which reimagines a classic gang film with women in the lead roles?
questions.funfact: Warriors is based on the 1979 cult film The Warriors and was developed with playwright Eisa Davis. It grew out of a 2024 concept album and is set to open at the Lunt-Fontanne Theatre in April 2027.

questions.text: What unit is used to measure electric current?
questions.funfact: The ampere, or amp, is named after the French physicist André-Marie Ampère. One amp is a flow of roughly 6.24 quintillion electrons past a point every second.

questions.text: Which TV show signs off its episodes with 'XOXO'?
questions.funfact: Gossip Girl's anonymous narrator signs off with 'XOXO, Gossip Girl', and the voice was provided by Kristen Bell. The show was based on Cecily von Ziegesar's book series and ran from 2007 to 2012.

questions.text: Which country won the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.funfact: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final on 19 July 2026 for their second World Cup, after their 2010 triumph. It was the first World Cup with 48 teams, co-hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico.

questions.text: The Japanese philosophy of wabi-sabi finds beauty in what?
questions.funfact: Wabi-sabi finds beauty in things that are imperfect, impermanent and incomplete, like a cracked tea bowl. It is tied to Japanese tea culture and Zen Buddhism, and the related art of kintsugi repairs broken pottery with gold.

questions.text: Which of these lakes is a source of the Nile?
questions.funfact: Lake Victoria feeds the White Nile and Ethiopia's Lake Tana is the source of the Blue Nile. The two meet at Khartoum in Sudan.

questions.text: How many people are in Leonardo da Vinci's painting The Last Supper? (Digits only)
questions.funfact: The painting shows Jesus with his twelve apostles, who react in groups of three. Leonardo painted it in the 1490s on the wall of a dining hall in Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan, and it survived the bombing of the building in World War II.

questions.text: What is Melba toast?
questions.funfact: Melba toast is sliced very thin and baked until crisp and dry. It is named after the Australian soprano Dame Nellie Melba, as is the dessert Peach Melba.

questions.text: Whose Eras Tour became the first concert tour to gross over US$2 billion?
questions.funfact: The Eras Tour ran from March 2023 to December 2024 across 149 shows and grossed more than US$2 billion.

questions.text: Which of these blood components is the largest?
questions.funfact: White blood cells can be around twice the width of red blood cells, but they are far outnumbered by them. Platelets are not whole cells at all, just tiny fragments of larger cells.

questions.text: Which of these countries has the UK's Union Jack in its flag?
questions.funfact: Fiji and Tuvalu both carry the Union Jack in the corner of their flags, alongside Australia and New Zealand. Canada's red ensign had one until 1965, when the maple leaf flag replaced it.

questions.text: Guess the year: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon, the Woodstock festival took place, and The Beatles released the album Abbey Road.
questions.funfact: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon on 20 July 1969, and Woodstock drew around 400,000 people that August. The famous zebra-crossing photo for Abbey Road was taken on 8 August 1969.

questions.text: In internet slang, what does the K stand for in AFAIK?
questions.funfact: AFAIK means 'as far as I know', and it is used when you are not completely sure of something. It is often paired with other chat shorthand such as IIRC (if I recall correctly) and IMHO (in my humble opinion).

questions.text: What Gen Alpha slang word, often used about delicious food, means 'really great'? (Hint: it starts with B)
questions.funfact: 'Bussin'' is slang for something excellent, especially food, and spread widely on TikTok in the early 2020s. Oxford chose another bit of internet slang, 'rizz', as its 2023 Word of the Year.

questions.text: From which sport does the term 'hospital pass' originate?
questions.funfact: A hospital pass leaves the receiver about to be flattened by a tackle. The phrase comes from rugby and is now used in Aussie rules, soccer and many other sports.

questions.text: Robert Galbraith is the pen name of which famous author?
questions.funfact: Rowling wrote the Cormoran Strike detective novels as Robert Galbraith, and the secret came out in July 2013, only months after The Cuckoo's Calling was published. Stephen King's famous pen name was Richard Bachman.

questions.text: Name 5 countries whose names have only one syllable.
questions.funfact: Chad, France, Greece, Laos and Spain are among the very few sovereign countries whose English names are a single syllable. Most countries, like Peru, Mali and Cuba, take two or more.

questions.text: Which famous music artist helps decide who performs at the NFL's Super Bowl halftime shows?
questions.funfact: Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has worked with the NFL as a live-music and entertainment strategist since 2019, and has helped shape the halftime show ever since.

questions.text: Which band released the 2009 single 'Heads Will Roll'?
questions.funfact: The New York indie rock band is fronted by Karen O. 'Heads Will Roll' comes from their 2009 album It's Blitz! and was remixed by DJ A-Trak.

questions.text: True or False: is a worm a mammal?
questions.funfact: Worms are invertebrates with no backbone, while mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates that feed their young milk. An earthworm even has five pairs of 'hearts', though they are really tubes called aortic arches.

questions.text: Which of these car brands is NOT named after a person or family: Toyota, Honda, Suzuki or Kia?
questions.funfact: Kia's name roughly means 'rise out of Asia'. Honda is named after founder Soichiro Honda, Suzuki after Michio Suzuki, and Toyota after the founding Toyoda family, with the spelling changed for luck.

questions.text: Odd one out: which of these is NOT one of the five Great Lakes of North America?
questions.funfact: The five Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario, often remembered with the acronym HOMES. Together they hold about a fifth of the world's surface fresh water.

questions.text: What is the name of the delivery spaceship piloted by Leela in Futurama?
questions.funfact: Futurama is set in the 31st century and follows the crew of Planet Express, a delivery company run by Professor Farnsworth. It was created by Simpsons creator Matt Groening and premiered in 1999.

questions.text: True or False: identical twins have the same fingerprints.
questions.funfact: Identical twins share the same DNA, but fingerprints form in the womb and are shaped by things like position and the fluid around the fingers. Twins' prints can look similar, but they are never identical.

questions.text: What is the name of the holy book that Muslims follow?
questions.funfact: The Quran is divided into 114 chapters called surahs, and Muslims believe it was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad over about 23 years. The word means 'recitation'.

questions.text: What colour are jeans that have not been treated or dyed?
questions.funfact: Natural cotton is a creamy off-white, so truly undyed denim looks beige or ecru instead of blue. The classic blue comes from indigo dye.

questions.text: What do you call the middle part of a Venn diagram, where the circles overlap?
questions.funfact: The overlap is called the intersection, and everything inside both circles combined is the union. Venn diagrams are named after the English logician John Venn, who introduced them in 1880.
